transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for seeing me. 

Um, I’m here because... well, I hope I don't sound difficult or anything, but for a few months now, I’ve just been noticing this... pattern. I supervise an administrative office, so I'm very used to keeping track of details, you know? And lately, my sister’s appointments keep getting moved without me knowing, and her bills are showing up wrong, and people just conveniently "forget" to call me back. 

Everyone keeps telling me it’s just innocent clerical mistakes, and I really try to be understanding, I do. But... I just know they’re keeping information from me. It really feels like they're working together to push me out of the decisions regarding her. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you believe for certain that people are deliberately working together against you?

Well... I know it sounds a bit harsh when you put it like that, and I really hate to think the worst of people. I always try to give everyone the benefit of the doubt, I promise. 

But... yes. Like I was just saying about her appointments getting shuffled and the bills showing up wrong... even when everyone insists to me that it’s just innocent mistakes, I just know they are keeping information from me. I am certain they are trying to push me out of the decisions regarding her care. 

I hope saying that doesn't make me sound paranoid or difficult. I'm really just trying to be completely honest with you... is it okay that I'm explaining it this way?
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I've never experienced anything like that, thank goodness. I know that's something people worry about with... well, with mental health things, but my mind is perfectly clear in that way. It's just the things I can actually see happening with the paperwork and the schedules. 

I'm completely grounded in reality, I promise. Does that help clear things up? I want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
If someone showed you clear proof that these scheduling and billing problems were simple mistakes, would you be able to accept that?

Well... I really, really wish I could. I know it would make everything so much easier for everyone, and I hate being the person who causes a fuss. I really try to be agreeable. 

But... even if someone showed me what looked like proof... I just couldn't accept it. I know that probably sounds stubborn, and I'm so sorry, I don't mean to be difficult at all. It's just that I've been seeing this pattern for months. The moved appointments, the incorrect bills, the unreturned calls... it's all too consistent. Even when everyone insists it's just a series of innocent mistakes, I just... I know in my heart they're keeping information from me. I know they're working together to push me out of the decisions regarding my sister. 

I hope you're not upset with me for saying that. I know it's not what people usually want to hear, but I promised to be completely honest with you. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you been diagnosed with any neurological or other medical illness that you think might be related to these experiences?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't. I'm actually very healthy, thankfully. I've always made a point to stay on top of my annual physicals and everything, especially since I spend so much time at a desk managing the office. You really have to take care of yourself, you know? 

But no, I don't have any neurological conditions or... or any medical illnesses like that at all. My regular doctor says I'm doing really well for fifty-nine. So there's definitely no medical issue that would be confusing my thinking or causing me to imagine things, if that's what you mean. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I just want to reassure you that my mind and my body are completely fine. Does that help rule things out for your notes? I want to be as helpful as I can.
Aside from this situation with your sister’s care, have you noticed yourself becoming less interested in things you usually enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I still enjoy my usual things. I mean, I still love gardening on the weekends, and I still read my mystery novels before bed. I try to keep up with all of that, I really do. 

I suppose maybe I've been a little... well, a little distracted lately, just because of everything going on with the clinic and my sister. It takes up a lot of my mental energy, trying to keep track of all the paperwork and making sure they aren't trying to pull a fast one. So maybe I haven't been quite as focused on my hobbies as I usually am. But I certainly haven't lost interest in them! 

I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression. I'm still very active and engaged with my life, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it well enough.
Before the issues with your sister began, have you generally tended to mistrust other people and suspect that they might take advantage of you?

Oh, no, definitely not! I've always prided myself on being a very trusting person, actually. I really try to see the best in everyone. 

In my line of work—managing the office—you have to be able to trust your team, and I've always had wonderful relationships with my coworkers and friends. I'm usually the one organizing the office potlucks and making sure everyone feels included. I would never just assume someone was out to get me or take advantage. That's just not who I am at all. 

That's why this whole situation with the clinic has been so upsetting for me. It's completely out of the ordinary for me to feel this way about people. I really wish I didn't have to be so suspicious of them, but... well, they've just given me no choice, with how they're acting. 

But generally speaking? Oh, no, I'm very trusting. I hope that doesn't make me sound naive! I just prefer to be positive. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what I'm usually like.
Have you felt that anyone can control your thoughts or put thoughts into your mind?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, nothing like that. That sounds... well, that sounds very frightening, to be honest. 

I've never felt like anyone was controlling my thoughts or putting things in my head. My thoughts are completely my own. Even with everything going on with the clinic and all the stress it's causing me, I know exactly what I'm thinking and why I'm thinking it. I'm just trying to be a good sister and protect her, you know? 

But no, nobody is controlling my mind. I'm very grounded in reality, I promise. I hope that's reassuring to hear? I wouldn't want you to think I was losing touch with myself or anything like that. I'm still very much in control of my own mind.
Have you had times when your speech or behavior became so disorganized that other people had trouble understanding you or found you acting very strangely?

Oh, dear, no. I really hope I haven't given you that impression! I'm very put together, I assure you. 

I mean, outside of dealing with my sister’s appointments and... well, trying to get straight answers from those people at the clinic, everything else is perfectly normal. I still keep my home in order, I pay all my bills on time, and I go to work and manage the office just like I always have. 

I suppose some people might think I’m a little... too focused on this whole clinic situation. But I'm certainly not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. I'm very capable and organized. 

I just want to make sure you know that I'm functioning perfectly well. I'm just being a responsible advocate for my sister. Does that make sense? I really hope you can see that I'm managing everything else just fine.
Have these beliefs about the clinic been present for longer than one month?

Well, yes, it has been a while now. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm dwelling on things too much, but... it's been about 11 months. 

It all started when my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse. It was quite a shock, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. I just wanted to make sure she was getting the best possible treatment, you know? But that's when I started noticing... well, the inconsistencies with the clinic. 

So, yes, about 11 months. I know that sounds like a long time to be dealing with this sort of stress, but when it's family, you just do what you have to do. I hope you can understand why I've been so persistent about it for so long. Is it okay that I've been keeping such close track of the timeline? I just want to be as helpful and accurate as possible for you.
